analysis.title: What Matters Today: AI Funding Concerns, Circuit breakers in Korea overnight, Core CPI Above Expectations, Estimating 0.32% for September Core PCE
key_insights: GS's global neocloud basket is down 20% in five sessions, roughly a 1st percentile move over ten years, with selling accelerating. Credit spreads have widened across the AI ecosystem, and hyperscaler IG spreads widened another 7.4bp last week.
If appetite to finance the AI buildout is constrained, the consequence is incrementally slower chip consumption, less capex and ultimately weaker growth.

Rich Privo says this is not fundamentally a demand crisis: aggregate token consumption continues to surprise to the upside. He argues demand for compute can grow exponentially but the capital available to finance it cannot.

Privo says the harder constraint to falsify is physical delivery (power, energizing data centers, gigawatts), which becomes more tangible into 2027 and 2028. He frames these as supply constraints, not evidence that demand is disappearing, and says they explain the derating across the complex.

Privo says the equilibrium favours owners of powered capacity with strong balance sheets over leveraged middlemen. He asks whether hyperscalers will fund capacity from equity and operating cash flow rather than debt, which would ease debt overhang concerns.

Privo says a lot of bad news is now priced: quality has rallied in 16 of 18 sessions with RSI at 83, discretionary net exposure is low, and rates are rallying. His gut is the market has overreacted in pockets, while credit's warning should still be respected.

Korea circuit breakers triggered for the first time since 7/29. KOSPI extended losses for a 7th consecutive session, the longest losing streak since September 2024. SK Hynix closed -11.1% and Samsung -9.5%.

GS's Korea desk attributes the timing to removal of the corporate bid: Samsung Electronics completed its buyback program on October 6 and SK Hynix is tapering. Foreign institutional selling (~80-87% concentrated in the two chip heavyweights) cleared into an empty domestic bid, broke psychological thresholds and triggered forced margin liquidations.

GS's trading desk saw no concentrated degrossing or capitulation in memory. The desk was 1.2x better sellers by end of day, with outflows less memory-concentrated than in the July drawdown and small pockets of dip buying in Memory, Power Grids and Holdcos.

Per exchange data, foreigners were net sellers for an 8th consecutive day, with Tech 86% of the selling (-$11.6bn in Tech and -$13.4bn in KOSPI over 8 sessions). Foreigners extended net-selling streaks to 15 days in Hynix and 12 days in Samsung Electronics (SEC).

September core CPI rose 0.33% m/m, above expectations. OER rose 0.35% m/m, contributing about 5bp more to core than GS expected, with the strength concentrated in the Midwest (+0.68%, SA by GS). Travel services, autos and recreation goods were also firm.

Based on CPI details, GS estimates September core PCE rose 0.32% m/m (vs. its 0.20% expectation before the CPI release), a year-over-year rate of +3.09%. The revision reflects upside surprises to OER, hotels and recreation forecasts.

market_movers.rationale: SK Hynix closed -11.1% as Korean circuit breakers triggered after the corporate buyback bid was removed and foreign selling continued. Foreigners have net sold for 15 straight days.
Samsung Electronics closed -9.5% after its buyback program finished October 6. Foreigners have net sold for 12 straight days.

sector_views.rationale: Leveraged middlemen face financing and delivery constraints, with the neocloud basket down 20% in five sessions. Privo favours owners of powered capacity with strong balance sheets, particularly well-capitalized hyperscalers.
Heavy foreign selling and forced margin liquidations, but the GS desk saw no capitulation or concentrated degrossing, and small pockets of dip buying appeared.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Above expectations, driven partly by firm shelter (OER). It feeds a higher core PCE estimate.
Contributed about 5bp more to core CPI than GS expected. The Midwest was +0.68% SA by GS, well above GS's estimate of trend.
GS estimate based on CPI details, up from the 0.20% it expected before the CPI release.
GS estimate implied by the 0.32% m/m core PCE estimate.

risk_factors: Constrained financing for the AI buildout could slow chip consumption and capex, and ultimately weaken growth.
Physical delivery risk (power, data center energization, permitting, policy) is expected to become more tangible into 2027 and 2028 and is likely to get messier given the political backdrop.
Widening credit spreads across the AI vertical, including hyperscaler IG spreads +7.4bp last week.
Continued foreign net selling in Korean tech now that the corporate bid has been removed, with risk of further margin liquidations.
A firmer core PCE print (0.32% estimated for September) as shelter strength persists.
vol_and_positioning: Quality has rallied in 16 of 18 sessions with RSI at 83. Discretionary net exposure is low, per Privo.
GS's Korea trading desk saw no concentrated degrossing or capitulation in memory and was 1.2x better sellers by end of day. Outflows were less memory-concentrated than in the July drawdown.

tension_points.bull_case: Privo says aggregate token consumption keeps surprising to the upside, so the demand story is intact. Bad news is now priced: neoclouds are down 20% in five sessions, discretionary net exposure is low, and rates are rallying, which improves the financing equation if they stabilize lower.
tension_points.bear_case: Credit is signalling stress: hyperscaler IG spreads widened another 7.4bp last week and spreads widened across the AI ecosystem. Capital to finance the buildout cannot grow as fast as compute demand, which could mean slower chip consumption, less capex and weaker growth.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Rates stabilizing lower would improve the financing equation, per Privo. Further credit spread widening would undercut his overreaction view.
